proof_summary: For the exceptional exponents, a modular analysis of padded decimal digits shows that a positive multiple of 27 or 81 whose reversal is also divisible has digit sum divisible by 27 or 81; below the respective all-nines candidate this forces every digit to be 9 (with the case of 9 immediate), proving the required minima. For every larger exponent, the palindrome built from one copy of the block 68899199886, or from \(3^{n-12}\) copies when \(n\ge12\), is divisible by \(3^n\): grouping its geometric block sum in thirds supplies successive factors of 3, and its length makes it strictly smaller than the all-nines number.
